task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 26, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style news update about the Larch Hollow Food Cooperative's decision to replace a future member rebate with selected shelf-price reductions.

facts.text: Members voting at Larch Hollow Food Cooperative approved a pricing change 280-90 on Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026.
The vote authorizes ending the rebate on purchases made after Oct. 1 and redirecting its planned budget to selected staple-food prices.
Rebate credits already earned will remain redeemable under their existing expiration dates.
The cooperative has approximately 6,800 members; 370 cast ballots in this vote.
Last year's rebate distributed $54,000 in credits, based on members' eligible purchases.
The board plans a $54,000 price-reduction budget for the coming year but has not selected the final item list.
Reduced shelf prices will apply to members and nonmembers alike.
The cooperative's annual membership fee will remain $20, with voting rights and workshop discounts retained.
Manager Edda Pike said the cooperative will compare item-level sales and gross margins before expanding the list.
The cooperative has no household-level estimate showing which shoppers will save more than their former rebate.
A shopper's outcome will depend on eligible past purchases and whether the shopper buys the newly discounted items.
Member Oren Lusk said his rebate had helped pay for a large winter grocery trip.
Lusk said, "A little off a shelf price does not arrive in one envelope when the heating bill does."
Nonmember customer Cira Venn said she shops there for basic ingredients but cannot regularly spend enough to justify membership for rebates alone.
Venn said, "I can use a lower price today without waiting to become somebody's loyal customer."
The cooperative reported an operating surplus of $61,000 last year before distributing rebate credits.
The board says the new budget is not an additional $54,000 on top of an unchanged rebate program.
The vote requires a member review after 12 months; it does not promise that the scheme will continue permanently.
The store began as a bulk-buying club in 1989 and still keeps a noticeboard for member recipes and classes.
No decision has been made to reduce wages, alter supplier payment periods or sell the cooperative.

forbidden_additions: All members voted or every household is guaranteed greater savings
Existing earned credits are canceled or two separate $54,000 programs will operate
